{{Top|leg|notoc=1}}
The '''Canons of Honor''' were a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] text of law and behavior.<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> Evolving from the ancient [[Mandalorian religion|religious]] laws followed by the [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] society that founded the Mandalorian culture, the Canons of Honor aimed at helping the [[Mandalorian Crusaders|ancient Mandalorian]] [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] attain glory and personal honor.<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> The Canons' texts were extrapolated from the ''[[Resol'nare]]'', the six central tenets of the Mandalorian culture. By following the tenets of the ''Resol'nare'',<ref name="GaW" /> with special emphasis placed upon loyalty to one's clan and engaging in combat, the laws of the Canons were satisfied, and a warrior earned honor.<ref name="HotM" />

Over [[Time/Legends|time]], the observance of the Canons of Honor waned.<ref name="HotM" /> The [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]], a peaceful sect of Mandalorian pacifists, rejected the warrior codes altogether following their rise<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> in the aftermath of the [[Mandalorian Excision]].<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> The Canons were revived, however, following the ascent of [[Jaster Mereel]] to the role of ''[[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor]]'',<ref name="GaW" /> the traditional ruler of the Mandalorian clans.<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> Mereel resurrected and modernized the tenets of the Canons of Honor when [[Gender/Legends|he]] established the [[Supercommando Codex]], a new set of guidelines for Mandalorian behavior,<ref name="GaW" /> stating that any Mandalorians who wished to fight would do so simply as highly-[[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|paid]] soldiers, and should conduct themselves as honorable [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]].<ref name="OpenSeasons">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 1|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 1]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Canons of Honor were first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe via a mention in the [[Star Wars Insider]] article [[The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors|''The History of the Mandalorians'']], [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Abel G. Peña]] and published [[March]] [[2005]] as part of the Insider magazine's [[Star Wars Insider 80|eightieth issue]]. The ''[[Galaxy at War]]'' reference book, written by [[Daniel Wallace]], later mentioned the Canons again, connecting the ancient code with the Supercommando Codex, when it was published on [[September 15]], [[2009]].

In the fifteenth episode of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]], entitled "[[Shades of Reason]]," the character [[Almec/Legends|Almec]] makes mention of a set of "ancient laws of Mandalore" the Death Watch hold themselves to. While the Death Watch have been established as followers of the Mandalorians' conqueror roots in pre-existing sources such as the [[Star Wars: Jango Fett: Open Seasons|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series, no official word has connected these ancient laws with the Canons of Honor, leaving the relationship between the two concepts possible but canonically uncertain.
